gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two leading 65% boards quote battery life on bases that only line up with the lights on: NuPhy rates the Air65 V3 (2,500 mAh) at up to 761 h lights off and 15-67 h lights on, the Lofree Flow 2 68 (2,000 mAh, not the 84's 3,000 mAh) is listed at up to 90 h off and 13 h on, and both are listed at the same 635 g.
standout_why: Compared against keebscout's low-profile guide, mkbguide's 65% list and ChatGPT's own answer text; the RTINGS pages (best low-profile, Air75 V3 vs K5 Max compare, Flow 2 review, Air75 V3 review) returned only navigation to my fetches, so I could not read their bodies and the score is capped at 2. Keebscout gives no battery, weight or height figure for the Air65 V3 or the Flow 2 68 (it only says '68- and 100-key versions also exist'). Mkbguide's 65% page lists no wireless low-profile board at all. ChatGPT's answers never mention battery and call the Lofree 'heavier to carry', and say RTINGS tested the larger sizes, whose batteries differ.
decides: It confirms the NuPhy Air65 V3 as the pick for anyone using it wirelessly with lights off (about 8.5 times the rated hours on 1.25 times the capacity). With lights on the gap shrinks to 15-67 h against 13 h, so both need charging every few days at 8 h a day. It removes 'the Lofree is heavier to carry' as a tiebreak, since both are listed at 635 g; the Lofree's case for itself is the aluminum body, VIA and shine-through legends, on a shorter 2.8 mm travel against NuPhy's 3.5 mm. The Keychron K7 Pro is not like-for-like: Bluetooth and cable only, 1,550 mAh. Caveat: all three makers' stores returned HTTP 429 to every read today, so these figures come from named reviewers and one retailer spec table, not the makers' pages.

findings.label: Battery capacity and rated hours (maker's claim as relayed by reviewers)
findings.value: 2,500 mAh; up to 761 h lights off; 15-67 h RGB on
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air65 V3 Review: The Best Compact Low-Profile… (GamePadSquire Test Desk, updated Aug 15, 2026)
findings.note: GamePadSquire's spec table: '2500mAh, up to 761h claimed (RGB off); 15-67h (RGB on)'. It labels these as claims, not its own measurement. Connection mode for the claim is not stated on this page. Arithmetic: 761 h / 8 h a day = 95 days; 15-67 h = 1.9-8.4 days.

findings.label: Rated battery life, lights off (second reviewer)
findings.value: up to 761 h with lighting disabled
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air65 V3 Review: A Smooth, Customizable Low-Profile Keyboard - MacSources (Christian Wood, 2026-10-07)
findings.note: MacSources: 'NuPhy rates battery life at up to 761 hours with lighting disabled.' The reviewer did not measure battery life.

findings.label: Battery capacity and rated hours, 68-key size
findings.value: 2,000 mAh; up to 90 h all lights off; up to 13 h all lights on
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow 2 68 Tri-Mode Wireless Low Profile Mechanical Keyboard (Geekbuying spec table)
findings.note: Retailer spec table, not Lofree's own page (lofree.co returned HTTP 429 on every attempt). The table does not say which connection mode the hours apply to. Arithmetic: 90 h / 8 h a day = 11 days; 13 h = 1.6 days.

findings.label: Battery by size: the 68 has a smaller cell than the 84 and 100
findings.value: 68-key: 2,000 mAh, 90 h; 84/100-key: 3,000 mAh, 120 h backlight off, about 17 h on
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow 2 Review (GamePadSquire Test Desk, updated Nov 24, 2026)
findings.note: GamePadSquire's spec table, maker ratings. A battery figure carried over from a Flow 2 84 or 100 review overstates the 68 by 1,000 mAh and 30 rated hours. The page also relays PC Gamer's drain result (about 22 h from 90% at maximum backlight) for a larger unit, not the 68.

findings.label: Normalised battery comparison, Air65 V3 against Flow 2 68
findings.value: Lights off: 761 h vs 90 h (8.5 times) on 2,500 vs 2,000 mAh (1.25 times). Lights on: 15-67 h vs 13 h
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air65 V3 Review (GamePadSquire); Lofree figures from the Geekbuying spec table and GamePadSquire's Flow 2 review
findings.note: Arithmetic: 761/90 = 8.46; 2,500/2,000 = 1.25; hours per mAh lights off 0.304 vs 0.045 (6.8 times). The lights-on rows are not identical loads: NuPhy's is RGB under non-shine-through keycaps, Lofree's is white-only backlight under shine-through keycaps. Neither maker's test conditions (mode, brightness) could be read from its own page today.

findings.label: Stated weight, both 68-key boards
findings.value: NuPhy Air65 V3 635 g; Lofree Flow 2 68 635 g (0.635 kg)
findings.source_title: Geekbuying spec table (Lofree 0.635 kg); GamePadSquire Air65 V3 review (635 g); GamePadSquire Flow 2 review ('635g (68) / 745g (84) / 870g (100)')
findings.note: MacSources also gives the Air65 V3 as 'approximately 1.4 pounds' (about 635 g). ChatGPT's 'heavier to carry' fits the 745 g Flow 2 84, not the 68. Neither figure was read on the maker's own page today, and the identical number for two different boards deserves a re-check there.

findings.label: Stated thickness, not on a confirmed common basis
findings.value: NuPhy Air65 V3 318.9 x 109.0 x 13.2 mm; Lofree Flow 2 68 341.2 x 107 x 21.5 mm
findings.source_title: GamePadSquire Air65 V3 spec table; Geekbuying Flow 2 68 spec table
findings.note: Neither page says where the height is taken (front or rear, with or without keycaps), so 13.2 mm against 21.5 mm should not be printed as a like-for-like gap. The Lofree 341.2 mm width also needs checking: GamePadSquire gives 341 x 126 x 21.5 mm as the 84-key size.

findings.label: Switch travel and force
findings.value: Air65 V3: Gateron Low-Profile 3.0 nano, 3.5 mm total, about 1.7 mm actuation (Red), 42/45/50 gf (Blush/Red/Brown). Flow 2: Kailh x Lofree Cloud (Surfer/Void/Pulse), 2.8 mm travel, 40±10 gf
findings.source_title: GamePadSquire Flow 2 review and GamePadSquire Air65 V3 review (spec tables)
findings.note: The Lofree's total travel is 0.7 mm shorter. Geekbuying's table confirms 40±10 gf for the Flow 2 68. No actuation point is listed for the Lofree switches.

findings.label: Polling rate by connection mode
findings.value: Air65 V3 and Flow 2: 1,000 Hz on cable and 2.4 GHz, 125 Hz on Bluetooth
findings.source_title: MacSources Air65 V3 review (Christian Wood); GamePadSquire Flow 2 spec table
findings.note: MacSources: 'wired and 2.4GHz modes operate at up to a 1000Hz polling rate, while Bluetooth operates at 125Hz.' GamePadSquire for the Flow 2: '1000Hz (2.4GHz & wired); 125Hz (Bluetooth)', stated for all sizes. No difference between the two here.

findings.label: Remapping software
findings.value: Air65 V3: NuPhyIO (web, with offline client), no QMK/VIA per GamePadSquire. Flow 2: QMK firmware with VIA web app. Keychron K7 Pro: QMK firmware, Keychron Launcher web app
findings.source_title: GamePadSquire Air65 V3 and Flow 2 reviews; Keychron store listing for the K7 Pro
findings.note: Conflict: keeb-finder's Air65 V3 page (https://keeb-finder.com/keyboards/nuphy-air65-v3) says it supports QMK and VIA. GamePadSquire says no, and MacSources names only NuPhyIO. Settle this on NuPhy's page before printing.

findings.value: $66.49 (list $114.99), in stock; 65% ANSI; Bluetooth and cable only (no 2.4 GHz); 1,550 mAh; 436 g; 306 x 97.5 mm; QMK / Keychron Launcher; hot-swap on the hot-swappable version only
findings.source_title: Keychron K7 Pro QMK/VIA Wireless Custom Mechanical Keyboard (keychron.com store search result, via storecheck)

Keychron's 'Bluetooth; 1000 Hz polling rate' does not say which mode the 1,000 Hz applies to. No battery-hours figure appears in the listing text.
